card:question: Does GPU parallelism change how many of the 671 CAMELS catchments can get full Bayesian calibration instead of point optimization?
card:hypothesis: Each catchment calibrates independently, so GPU batching turns full Bayesian treatment of all 671 into a cheap throughput problem, not a blocker.
card:sequential_part: Each catchment's posterior waits on one chain's 100,000 serial proposal-accept steps; four chains per catchment.
card:method: none - the 671 catchments' four chains each are independent, so all 2,684 chains run side by side in one batched pass.
card:if_lever: One GPU gives >=20x over CPU and finishes all 671 in under an hour, so compute is the lever here.
card:if_not: Vectorized CPU finishes all 671 in a couple of hours, so throughput does not decide which catchments get full Bayesian treatment.
card:test_summary: Time full Bayesian MCMC (4 chains x 1e5 iterations, R-hat<1.2) for 671 CAMELS catchments on one GPU versus a vectorized CPU and versus point optimization; measure whether GPU throughput decides how many catchments get full Bayesian treatment.
card:closest_prior: Freitas et al. 2022 GPU-optimized a hydrological model's calibration to 20x CPU speedup, on one distributed model, not batched MCMC across many GR4J catchments [s_mgb].
card:left_open: No published result times batched GPU MCMC giving all 671 CAMELS catchments full Bayesian GR4J treatment, so the crossover is unmeasured [s_mgb].
card:anchor: Reproduce airGR's GR4J: parameter set X=(165.05, 6.46, 422.50, 2.45) gives calibration NSE 0.495 on its example basin [s_airgr_nse].
card:limits: Shows GR4J only, not expensive distributed or hierarchical models; US CAMELS unless the optional global stretch runs; nothing about single-chain mixing limits.
